Article Title: India vs New Zealand: How weather spoilt families' day out in Hamilton
Article Text:
The third ODI between India and New Zealand at Seddon Park in Hamilton was washed out. (Image: Sahil Malhotra/TimesofIndia.com)

The Indian team bus was mobbed by fans repeatedly during the third ODI between India and New Zealand in Hamilton. (Image: Sahil Malhotra/TimesofIndia.com)

HAMILTON: Around 2:30 PM local time, 30 minutes before the official start time for the third ODI, the Indian team bus arrived at the Seddon Park in Hamilton. When the doors opened, the assembled Indian fans were in for a surprise. With their phones pointed to the bus, expecting the entire squad to emerge, the first, and only, player to emerge for a discussion with the local and India's operations teams was former India captain Rohit Sharma . After a long chat, Rohit sprinted to the stadium and did not return for close to 15 minutes.With the door closed, the players continued to sit inside waiting for the go-ahead from the team management. Rohit finally returned to the bus amid loud chants but none of the players got down as another discussion ensued. It was later learnt that if the players had entered the Players and Match Officials Area (PMOA), they wouldn't have been allowed to exit and re-enter as per the guidelines. So a decision to return to the team hotel was taken as drizzle continued and the ground remained far from ready.Before the team bus could get going for the Indian team hotel, having waited for over half-an-hour, captain Shubman Gill , coach Gautam Gambhir and other support staff members joined New Zealand captain Mitchell Santner.The rest of the BlackCaps players who had arrived by their own cars, also waited outside the venue. When they didn't get the necessary go-ahead, they also began driving back to the team hotel.When the weather finally cleared and the outfield was prepared in lightning-quick time, the Indian team bus returned. Meanwhile, Rohit beat the pack as he travelled with New Zealand players in their car.It was a frustrating day of waiting, rain and chilly winds in Hamilton, and even more so for the numerous family members gathered in the hospitality box.From Rohit Sharma's wife Ritika to Shubman Gill and Arshdeep Singh's parents, all had taken their seats when the toss and revised timings were announced. Gill won another flip of the coin, and just when the Indian players started warming-up to get ready for action, another drizzle sent them off the field, never to return.Rohit would occasionally emerge from the dressing room to wave to his daughter in the stands and gestured to Gill Sr but even that didn't last long as the rain got heavier, forcing the players indoors and leaving match officials with the formal announcement to abandon the contest. When it was announced on the PA, the fans quickly rushed out to position themselves near the team bus, for the third time that day, and another surprise was in store. Virat Kohli , amid loud chants of "Radhe! Radhe!", left in a private car with Gill, Ishan Kishan and Naman Dhir. Even Rohit ditched the team bus and left in a car while the rest, featuring Shreyas Iyer, KL Rahul, coach Gambhir, boarded the team bus to end the long day of waiting and rain.For the fans, it was an afternoon spent soaking in the rain to catch a glimpse of their favourite cricketers and the maximum they got was a 10-second glimpse of the players entering and exiting their respective vehicles.
Article Summary: The third ODI between India and New Zealand at Seddon Park in Hamilton was washed out. The Indian team bus was mobbed by fans repeatedly during the match. Virat Kohli left in a private car with Shubman Gill, Ishan Kishan and Naman Dhir.

Article Title: Esha Singh leads India to team gold as Manu Bhaker joins her in 25m pistol final at ISSF World Championships
Article Text:
Esha Singh (PTI Photo)

Esha's strong comeback powers India

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

India eye another Olympic quota place

NEW DELHI: India enjoyed a memorable day at the ISSF World Championships on Tuesday as Esha Singh spearheaded the country's charge to the women's 25m pistol team gold, while also qualifying for the individual final alongside double Olympic medallist Manu Bhaker Esha, one of India's leading pistol shooters, topped the Indian trio in the two-day qualification round with a score of 590. Manu contributed 587 and Divya Subbaraju added 584 as India aggregated 1761 to clinch the gold medal.South Korea finished second with 1748 to take silver, while Vietnam claimed bronze with a total of 1745.The team triumph was complemented by Esha and Manu securing places in the individual final, giving India a double chance to fight for another medal and a quota place for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.The 21-year-old Esha finished third in the individual qualification standings with 590, behind Germany's Doreen Vennekamp, who topped the field with 592 to equal the Olympic record, and Hungary's Veronika Major, who shot 591.Esha produced an impressive recovery in Tuesday's Rapid round after managing 292 in Monday's Precision round. She shot series of 100, 98 and 100 to register 298 in the Rapid round and finish with an overall score of 590.Manu also bounced back after a modest 289 in the Precision round. The two-time Olympic medallist put together a series of 99, 99 and 100 in the Rapid round to finish sixth with 587 and secure her place among the eight finalists.Divya, meanwhile, narrowly missed out on the individual final, finishing 10th in the qualification standings with 584.The individual final presents India with an opportunity to add to its tally of Olympic quota places. The three medallists in the event will secure quota places for their respective countries, meaning India could potentially claim two if both Esha and Manu finish on the podium.Jaypal Malviya has already opened India's account in the Olympic qualification race at the championships. He won silver in the men's 10m air pistol to become the country's first shooter to secure a quota place for the Los Angeles Games at the event.The women's 25m pistol team gold and the presence of two Indian shooters in the individual final provide a significant boost to India's campaign.
Article Summary: India win women's 25m pistol team gold at ISSF World Championships. Esha Singh and Manu Bhaker also qualify for individual final. Team triumph gives India a double chance to fight for another medal and a quota place for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.

Article Title: '55-45 for Javokhir Sindarov': Russian GM Peter Svidler gives World Chess C'ship challenger narrow edge over D Gukesh
Article Text:
Gukesh Dommaraju and Javokhir Sindarov

Gukesh aims to defend World Chess Championship title

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Russian Grandmaster Peter Svidler believes Javokhir Sindarov holds a slight advantage over reigning world champion D Gukesh ahead of their upcoming World Championship match but feels it would be unfair to give the Uzbek a significantly higher edge.Speaking to FIDE, Svidler gave Sindarov a 55-45 advantage, while stressing that Gukesh's experience and ability in the unique World Championship format should not be underestimated.“For this match, 60% [for Javokhir Sindarov] is already very high. Even with the kind of a year and a half Gukesh has had, I don’t think going higher than 55 is justifiable," Svidler said.“He’s still a very strong player, it’s still a very specific format. So, I’m kind of willing to go 55-45 for Sindarov, but I don’t think I’m willing to go higher."Gukesh, meanwhile, is gearing up for the biggest challenge of his career as he prepares to defend his world title against Sindarov in a 14-game classical chess match scheduled from November 24 to December 12 in Geneva, Switzerland.The 20-year-old Indian recently visited the famous Tirumala Sri Venkateswara Swamy Temple in Andhra Pradesh to seek blessings ahead of the title defence.The visit came days after he also offered prayers at Neem Karoli Baba's ashram.The upcoming contest will be historic, with both players set to be 20 years old when the match begins, making it the youngest World Championship encounter in chess history.Gukesh made history in December 2024 when he defeated China's Ding Liren to become the youngest undisputed World Chess Champion at the age of 18 years, six months and 24 days. He also became only the second Indian, after Viswanathan Anand, to claim the prestigious title.The championship will feature a maximum of 14 classical games, with the first player to reach 7.5 points being crowned champion. If the scores are level at 7-7, the title will be decided through tiebreaks.The opening ceremony is scheduled for November 22, while the first classical game will be played on November 24 at the Fondation Martin Bodmer in Cologny, Geneva. The final classical game is scheduled for December 11, with December 12 reserved for a possible tiebreak.The championship carries a total prize fund of $2.5 million, with each player receiving $200,000 for every game won and the remaining prize money to be shared equally.
Article Summary: Russian Grandmaster Peter Svidler believes Javokhir Sindarov holds a slight advantage over reigning world champion D Gukesh. The 20-year-old Indian is gearing up for the biggest challenge of his career as he prepares to defend his world title. The 14-game classical chess match is scheduled from November 24 to December 12 in Geneva, Switzerland.

Article Title: Fresh Sandpapergate storm puts Mitchell Starc in spotlight; Alyssa Healy reveals her stance: 'Slightly conflicted'
Article Text:
Alyssa Healy (Photo/Getty Images)

Alyssa Healy reacts to fresh Sandpapergate allegations involving Mitchell Starc

What is the Sandpapergate controversy?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Healy urges empathy for those involved in Sandpapergate

The infamous Sandpapergate scandal has returned to haunt Australian cricket, with fresh claims from former batter Usman Khawaja reigniting debate over the 2018 ball-tampering controversy. This time, the spotlight has fallen on Mitchell Starc, with his wife and former Australia women's captain Alyssa Healy admitting that she feels "slightly conflicted" about the renewed allegations.Khawaja, in his newly released autobiography Sabr, made explosive revelations about the 2018 Cape Town Test against South Africa, claiming that the entire Australian Test team was aware of the use of sandpaper to tamper with the ball. He also alleged that ball-tampering was not restricted to the infamous third Test, with the practice reportedly taking place during the second Test of the series as well.Starc, however, has firmly rejected Khawaja's claims, maintaining that he stands by the joint statement released in 2021 alongside Pat Cummins, Josh Hazlewood and Nathan Lyon. The four Australian fast bowlers had denied knowing about the sandpaper being taken onto the field and the ball being tampered with during the Cape Town Test.Speaking at Kayo Sports and Fox Cricket's launch event, Healy admitted that the situation was difficult for her to comment on, given her personal connection to the controversy."It's a hard one to comment on. At the moment, I feel slightly conflicted, and I'm in the middle of it. It's hard to make a comment on it, we'll see where it goes and if CA do take it forward or how it rolls throughout the media, and I'll make a comment from there. For now, I'm just gonna sit and wait and watch it unfold," Healy said.Her comments come after Starc publicly pushed back against Khawaja's version of events, insisting that his position on the controversy remains unchanged.The Sandpapergate scandal dates back to the third Test between Australia and South Africa at Newlands, Cape Town, in March 2018. During the match, television cameras captured Cameron Bancroft using a piece of sandpaper to alter the condition of the ball.The incident triggered one of the biggest controversies in Australian cricket history. Bancroft was handed a nine-month suspension, while then-captain Steve Smith and vice-captain David Warner received 12-month bans from international and domestic cricket. Smith was also removed from the captaincy, while Warner was banned from holding a leadership position in Australian cricket.Khawaja's latest revelations have brought the episode back into the spotlight, with questions being raised about how widespread the knowledge of the ball-tampering operation was within the Australian dressing room.However, Cricket Australia chief executive Todd Greenberg has indicated that the governing body has little interest in reopening the matter more than eight years after the incident. Healy backed that approach, suggesting that Australian cricket should focus on moving forward rather than revisiting a controversy that had already left a lasting impact on those involved."I watched it eight years ago too. I think the game of cricket as a whole has moved on. (Cricket Australia CEO) Todd Greenberg's statement today about not looking into it any further is a great sign of where we're headed and that's moving forward and looking ahead to this summer," she said.She said the individuals mentioned in Khawaja's book were being forced to revisit difficult memories and urged people to consider the emotional toll of the renewed scrutiny."I feel for everyone involved. I know a human element in it as well that people are being dragged back through some things and reliving some memories. I think from a human side of things we've got to remember that and put our arms around the people that are being mentioned," she added.
Article Summary: Alyssa Healy reacts to fresh Sandpapergate allegations involving Mitchell Starc. Former Australia women's captain says she feels "slightly conflicted" about the renewed allegations. Comes after fresh claims from former batter Usman Khawaja reignited debate over the 2018 ball-tampering controversy.

NEW DELHI: In a boost to India’s Test team, Rishabh Pant is scheduled to leave for New Zealand on Thursday. Pant will undergo an obligatory match simulation session at the Centre of Excellence (CoE) on Wednesday.TOI understands that the CoE medical staff is satisfied with Pant’s recovery after the side strain he sustained during the Irani Cup in the first week of Oct.While the rest of the Test team has already assembled in New Zealand and getting game time before the two-Test series, Pant will have about a week to get ready for the first Test in Wellington starting on Nov 19.Pant had initially requested the selectors to pick him for the ongoing India ‘A’ tour in New Zealand to get into rhythm for the crucial series which could decide India’s fate in the World Test Championship (WTC).However, sources close to the team management claim that Pant is experienced enough to be ready for the first Test. “This is the first time in a long while that the Test players have got such extensive preparation time for an away Test series. Pant had been part of tours to Australia and England where the Indian team has played a Test match within one week of landing in the country,” a source told TOI.It will be interesting to see if the team management decides to go with Dhruv Jurel in the playing XI alongside Pant.
Article Summary: Rishabh Pant will undergo an obligatory match simulation session at the Centre of Excellence (CoE) on Wednesday. The CoE medical staff is satisfied with Pant’s recovery after the side strain he sustained during the Irani Cup in the first week of Oct.

Article Title: Dhinidhi Desinghu puts celebrations on hold, eyes LA Olympics
Article Text:
Dhinidhi Desinghu returned from Dakar, Senegal on Monday

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

BENGALURU: India’s teenage swimming sensation Dhinidhi Desinghu returned from Dakar, Senegal, on Monday morning to a warm welcome from officials of the Karnataka Swimming Association. After a traditional reception, she was felicitated at her home club, Dolphin Aquatics, at the Centre of Excellence (CoE).But after winning two landmark bronze medals at the Youth Olympics last week, celebrations were not high on the 15-year-old Bengaluru swimmer’s agenda. Her books were waiting.Although her parents urged her to take a day off and enjoy the Deepavali festivities, Dhinidhi wasted little time getting back to her studies and private tutorials. With her Class XI examinations at Kendriya Vidyalaya, DRDO , beginning on Nov 16, academics have taken priority once again.For the teenager, the discipline that has helped her make a mark in the swimming pool extends to the classroom too.“There is no time to celebrate because my examinations are coming up. I carried my books to Dakar also, but didn’t want to add to the stress and didn’t study,” said the teenager who won gold, silver and bronze in 200m, 100m and 400m freestyle events respectively at the Asian Age Group Championships in Bangkok in July this year.Her coach, Nihar Ameen, who was delighted by his ward’s success, told TOI, “She’s a talent we all know that—more than that, she is a hard worker. Talent alone doesn’t give you the results. At some point in time, you’ve got to break through the glass ceiling. And you’ve got to really work hard and only then go to the next level, and that’s what she’s doing.”Dhinindhi, who was the youngest in India’s Paris Olympics contingent, won the 100m freestyle bronze with a national record time of 56.27 seconds and finished the 200m freestyle event in 2:02.28 for the bronze medal.While the results are promising, Ameen said they are looking ahead to attaining the ‘A’ qualifying mark for the 2028 LA Olympics.“Much of the last couple of years we’ve been trying to get her to get to the point where she breaks two minutes and works towards the A qualifying time for the LA Olympics (1.56.43). It’s a Herculean task, but I’m glad she is ending the season on a high, you know,” stated the Dhronacharya awardee.While none of the female swimmers attained the qualifying mark set by the Swimming Federation of India for the recently concluded Asian Games , Ameen believes swimmers like Dhindhi should have been given an opportunity to compete against the best in Asia.“The best of the country need to be motivated. If our youngsters see that there are no swimmers (female) going to the Asian Games, Olympics or the Commonwealth Games, why would they stay in the course till they peak when they are 19 or 20 years old? The best in the country should have been sent, even for representation; on that count, I feel the federation made a grave error, and it impacted Dhinidhi psychologically,” pointed out Ameen.For Dhinidhi, the target is clear: qualifying for the LA Games.“My goal is to qualify for the Olympics. We are already towards the end of 2026, and the qualifiers start next year, so there isn’t much time. It is very difficult to qualify in the 100 and 200 metres freestyle events, but I will give my best,” she said.But for the next couple of weeks, the focus is on academics and not timing in the pool.
Article Summary: Dhinidhi Desinghu returned from Dakar, Senegal on Monday morning. The 15-year- old won two bronze medals at the Youth Olympics last week. Her coach, Nihar Ameen, is looking ahead to attaining the ‘A’ qualifying mark for the 2028 LA Olympics.

Article Title: Indian Super League brings hope to John Abraham amidst Indian football’s struggles
Article Text:
NorthEast United FC owner John Abraham

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

KOLKATA: It has not been a good year for Indian football.The first half of it was spent getting through an agreement between the clubs and the All India Football Federation (AIFF) for the organisation of the Indian Super League (ISL), the top-tier league in the country. The second half has already witnessed a star-studded line-up of international friendlies against giants like Brazil and Uruguay that brought some cheer for fans but came at the cost of India’s participation in the FIFA ASEAN Cup.It was in this backdrop that the 13th edition of ISL kicked off exactly a month ago with no official television broadcaster and matches being live-streamed on YouTube. This club-organised season arrived at a time when Indian football was witnessing a dip in popularity, with the national men’s team languishing at 138th in the FIFA rankings.Yet, the matches have lived up to their billing in terms of competitiveness and thrills, producing end-to-end football, late goals and moments of individual brilliance.And one man who sees the positives from the season so far is actor and NorthEast United FC owner John Abraham , whose optimism about footballing talent in the northeast has endured some rough seasons and ultimately helped make NEUFC a club to reckon with in ISL.“I’ve been watching all the games, and it’s been a lot of fun. The ratings on YouTube are shattering records, and that just shows that India is ready for football,” Abraham said after NEUFC’s match on Thursday.The Highlanders have enjoyed an unbeaten start to the season and sit second in the table, a point behind leaders Mohun Bagan Super Giant, with 11 points from five games.They, in fact, beat Mohun Bagan with a late strike in their opening match of the campaign.Although most stadiums still need more fans to be called a “packed house”, viewership for the live streams has been steadily growing.“We’re ready for Indian football, and I’m very excited. It’s only a matter of time, and I’m saying this as a prophecy, the stands are going to be full. The stands are going to fill up completely. So, all credit to all of us who are partaking in this process,” Abraham added.Only time will tell if his prophecy comes true, but all stakeholders in Indian football are keen to see it happen in the near future.
Article Summary: The 13th edition of ISL kicked off exactly a month ago with no official television broadcaster and matches being live-streamed on YouTube. This club- organised season arrived at a time when Indian football was witnessing a dip in popularity, with the national men’s team languishing at 138th in the FIFA rankings.

Article Title: Shourya Ambure wins historic bronze, India's first track and field medal at Dakar Youth Olympics
Article Text:
Shourya Ambure (Video grabs)

Two personal bests in a day

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

India's medal tally reaches eight

NEW DELHI: India's Shourya Ambure produced a memorable performance at the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games, winning a historic bronze medal in the women's 100m hurdles to deliver the country's first track and field medal at the ongoing edition on Sunday.The 17-year-old from Maharashtra clocked a personal best of 13.59 seconds to finish third in the final, narrowly missing out on the silver medal by just 0.02 seconds. China's Zhang Keyi clinched gold with a timing of 13.17 seconds, while France's Anna Peeters took silver in 13.57 seconds.Ambure's achievement was particularly significant as she was India's only track and field athlete competing at the Games. She also bettered her personal best twice on the same day, underlining her consistency and ability to deliver on the big occasion.Ambure had already set the tone in the semi-finals, clocking 13.77 seconds to qualify for the medal race. She then raised her performance in the final, shaving 0.18 seconds off that mark to secure a place on the podium.The Maharashtra sprinter's bronze adds another significant chapter to her growing career. In the space of just 18 months, she has won medals at the Asian U18 Championships, Asian Youth Games and Youth Olympic Games, establishing herself as one of India's promising young hurdlers.Her performance also provided a significant boost to India's athletics campaign in Dakar, with the youngster making the most of her opportunity as the country's sole representative in track and field.Ambure's bronze was India's eighth medal at the Dakar Youth Olympics, taking the country's tally to three silver and five bronze medals.Earlier, wrestler Taniya had secured India's first-ever beach wrestling medal at the Games, winning silver in the women's 75kg category. She lost 1-2 to China's Min Zhao, the 2025 U17 world champion in the 69kg category, in the gold medal bout. Taniya had defeated USA's Matilda Hruby 3-1 in the semi-finals.Other silver medallists for India include Khushbu Rajakbhai Darjada in women's 63kg judo and Tanvi Patri in badminton.Swimming also contributed three medals, with Dhinidhi Desinghu winning bronze in the women's 100m and 200m freestyle events, while Tirthank Pegu claimed bronze in the men's 200m butterfly. Desinghu became the first Indian to win multiple medals at a single Youth Olympics edition, while Pegu secured India's first-ever male swimming medal at the Games.Rajkumari Lanchenbi Chanu added another bronze in the women's changquan combined wushu event.
Article Summary: Shourya Ambure wins bronze in women's 100m hurdles at Dakar 2026 Games. The 17-year-old clocked a personal best of 13.59 seconds to finish third. China's Zhang Keyi clinched gold, while France's Anna Peeters took silver. India's medal tally reaches eight with three silver and five bronze medals.

Article Title: Diwali fireworks, rain force Chennai Open final between Janice Tjen and Magda Linette to be postponed
Article Text:
Chennai: Thick smog engulfs the SDAT Tennis Stadium caused by firecracker celebrations during Diwali, ahead of the singles final of the WTA 250 Chennai Open tennis tournament, in Chennai. (PTI Photo)

Tjen and Linette book final spots

Vaishnavi Adkar , Rutuja Bhosale finish runners-up

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The WTA 250 Chennai Open women's singles final between defending champion Janice Tjen and Poland's Magda Linette has been rescheduled for Monday after rain and deteriorating air quality forced organisers to postpone Sunday's title clash at the SDAT Tennis Stadium.The championship match, which was originally scheduled to take place on Sunday, could not get underway as rain interrupted play and smoke from Diwali fireworks affected the air quality around the venue. The organisers subsequently decided to push the contest back by a day, with the final now scheduled to begin at 11 am IST on Monday, November 9.Tjen, the top seed from Indonesia, was due to face third seed Linette in a clash between two players looking to add another milestone to their Chennai Open campaigns. However, the disruption meant the tournament's closing day ended without the much-anticipated singles showdown.The decision to stage the final on Diwali had already attracted criticism, with questions being raised over the organisers' choice of date given the traditional fireworks celebrations across Chennai.The impact of the celebrations was also felt during the semi-finals, when the sound of firecrackers bursting outside the stadium repeatedly disrupted proceedings.The noise became particularly pronounced on Sunday evening as Diwali celebrations gathered pace across the city.Such disturbances are especially challenging in tennis, where players need to maintain concentration and points are generally played in silence. While spectators can cheer between points, the repeated sounds of crackers in the vicinity of the stadium made it difficult to maintain the usual playing environment.Tjen will be aiming to defend the title she won last year after securing her place in a second successive Chennai Open final. The Indonesian top seed defeated American Robin Montgomery 6-3, 6-4 in the semi-finals to move within one win of retaining her crown.Linette, meanwhile, had to fight back after dropping the opening set against seventh seed Anastasia Zakharova. The Polish player recovered to register a 2-6, 6-2, 6-3 victory and set up the final against Tjen.The third seed will be hoping to go one step further this time after finishing runner-up at the Chennai Open in 2022.Earlier on Sunday, India's Vaishnavi Adkar and Rutuja Bhosale missed out on the women's doubles title after losing to Switzerland's Simona Waltert and Naima Karamoko in straight sets.The Indian combination endured a difficult outing, going down 2-6, 0-6 as the Swiss pair controlled the match from the outset. Karamoko was particularly effective at the net, while Waltert provided dependable support from the baseline.Waltert and Karamoko secured early breaks in both sets and maintained their advantage to complete a comfortable victory and lift the doubles trophy.Despite the defeat, Adkar and Bhosale had reason to take pride in their campaign. They became the first all-Indian pairing to reach a WTA Tour-level doubles final.The Indian duo had booked their place in the championship match by producing a strong performance against second seeds Weronika Falkowska of Poland and Alana Smith of the United States. They registered a 6-2, 2-6, [10-8] victory in the semi-finals before their run ended against the Swiss combination in the final.
Article Summary: The WTA 250 Chennai Open women's singles final has been rescheduled for Monday after rain and deteriorating air quality forced organisers to postpone Sunday's title clash. The decision to stage the final on Diwali had already attracted criticism, with questions being raised over the organisers' choice of date given the traditional fireworks celebrations across Chennai.

NEW DELHI: New Zealand have been forced into another squad reshuffle ahead of the third ODI against India, with mounting injury concerns threatening to disrupt their plans for the remainder of the series.Fast bowler Kristian Clarke has been called up as cover for Blair Tickner ahead of Tuesday's third ODI, while Lockie Ferguson has been ruled out of the fourth and fifth matches after failing to recover fully from a calf injury sustained during the T20I series.The latest developments add to New Zealand's growing list of fitness concerns, with Matt Henry also recovering from a concussion-related issue and Tickner required to undergo a mandatory stand-down period despite being cleared of concussion.Ferguson has been ruled out of the final two ODIs after failing to recover fully from a low-grade tear in his right calf. The injury was sustained during the T20I series against India.Tickner, meanwhile, was struck by a ball while batting during the second ODI. Although he has since been cleared of concussion, his replacement in the playing XI by Matt Fisher means he must observe the ICC's mandatory seven-day stand-down period from the date of the match before returning to international cricket.Northern Districts fast bowler Clarke has consequently been drafted into the squad to provide additional bowling cover for the third ODI.Henry's availability also remains a concern. Initially cleared of concussion following his collision with Devon Conway in Auckland, the fast bowler was reassessed in Wellington and advised to target a return for the fourth ODI.New Zealand have also adjusted their plans for the transition from the ODI series to the upcoming Test assignment.Henry and Kyle Jamieson, who were initially scheduled to join the Test camp in Wellington after the third ODI, will now remain with the ODI squad for the fourth match.Two additional players are also expected to be brought into the squad across the fourth and fifth ODIs, with the composition for the final match still to be confirmed.Meanwhile, Tom Latham, Daryl Mitchell, Henry Nicholls, Glenn Phillips and Nathan Smith will leave for Wellington on Wednesday to begin preparations for the Test series. New Zealand Cricket said the Test squad to face India would be announced in the coming days.
Article Summary: New Zealand have been forced into another squad reshuffle ahead of the third ODI against India. Fast bowler Kristian Clarke has been called up as cover for Blair Tickner. Lockie Ferguson has been ruled out of the fourth and fifth matches after failing to recover fully from a calf injury. Matt Henry also recovering from a concussion-related issue.

Legendary India batter Sunil Gavaskar has weighed in on the debate surrounding Virat Kohli 's pursuit of 100 international centuries, suggesting that a teammate making a personal sacrifice to help the star reach the landmark would bring joy to Indian cricket fans as well.Kohli was in superb touch during the first ODI against New Zealand, smashing 74 off just 51 deliveries to guide India towards victory in a low-scoring contest. However, Gavaskar raised an interesting possibility in his latest column for: had Kohli stayed at the crease for longer, captain Shubman Gill and vice-captain Shreyas Iyer could have found themselves in a difficult position.With India closing in on the target, the two batters might have had to choose between finishing the match quickly and giving Kohli an opportunity to reach his century. The prospect becomes even more significant given that Kohli is chasing the historic mark of 100 international hundreds.Gavaskar acknowledged that winning a match must remain the team's primary objective, but argued that helping a player achieve such a landmark, provided it does not compromise the result, could be a moment of collective celebration."Indians have always been fond of records and so there's always a debate about the rights and wrongs of going for it.One thing for sure that 99% of those who say they don't play for records are actually incapable talent and temperament wise of setting any and so it's easy for them to say so," Gavaskar wrote."There is not a single Indian cricket fan who does not want Kohli to get to 100 international centuries. We are all cheering for him to get there and so, if there's an occasion where some other teammate sacrifices his runs to allow him the chance to get there, the glory will not be just Kohli's but for all Indian cricket fans too," he added.Kohli eventually fell for 74 with India at 124/3 in the rain-affected contest, leaving the team with relatively little work to do in the chase. His dismissal also meant Gill and Iyer did not have to confront the possibility of managing the chase around his personal milestone.Gavaskar felt the two players were spared a potentially awkward situation, including the prospect of facing criticism from fans on social media if India had delayed sealing the victory to give Kohli a chance to complete his hundred."Kohli got out in the 70s. Gill and Iyer were thus spared any blowback if the winning runs had been hit with Kohli unbeaten in the 90s. Yes, it's a team game, but it's also good for the team if one of its members, especially a star player, gets to a personal milestone without affecting the team's chances of winning," Gavaskar pointed out.Kohli, who now plays only ODIs, has 86 international centuries to his name. Article Title: ‘He got greedy’: Ex-India captain's blunt take on Arshdeep Singh after four-wicket haul
Article Text:

Jadeja impressed with Anshul Kamboj

Former India cricketer Ajay Jadeja has praised Arshdeep Singh's overall performance in India's five-wicket victory over New Zealand in the first ODI in Auckland, but believes the left-arm pacer could have avoided an expensive finish to his spell.India began their five-match ODI series with a comfortable win at Eden Park on Wednesday, November 4. In a rain-interrupted contest reduced to 32 overs per side, New Zealand were bowled out for 185 before India chased down the revised target of 143 in just 22.4 overs. Virat Kohli led the chase with a fluent 74, while Shubman Gill contributed 37 as the duo stitched together a 113-run partnership. India eventually crossed the finish line with five wickets to spare and 56 deliveries remaining.With the ball, Arshdeep was India's leading wicket-taker, claiming four wickets in his 10 overs. However, his figures of 4/70 were inflated by an expensive final over in which New Zealand tailender Blair Tickner struck him for three sixes, taking 23 runs off the over.Assessing the pacer's performance, Jadeja felt Arshdeep had been impressive for most of his spell but allowed the opportunity to complete a five-wicket haul to influence his bowling towards the end."I would call him slightly greedy. He himself said that as well. If you remove his last over, he had dismissed four batters before that and had given 40-odd runs. He got slightly greedy for the fifth wicket in the last over," Jadeja said on Sony Sports Network.Arshdeep had himself admitted after the match that the fifth wicket would have been his favourite, indicating that he was keen to complete a five-wicket haul. Despite missing out on the milestone, his four-wicket effort placed him in an exclusive group of Indian fast bowlers to achieve the feat in an ODI in New Zealand, alongside Javagal Srinath and Mohammed Shami.Jadeja, however, stressed that the expensive final over should not overshadow what Arshdeep brings to India's bowling combination. He pointed to the value of having a left-arm fast bowler in an attack that already features Jasprit Bumrah, adding that the competition for places would only benefit the team."It happens. It's natural, but Arshdeep Singh is showing that he can play in ODIs as well, which I believe is a very good thing when a left-arm seamer gets added to this attack with (Jasprit) Bumrah. The competition has increased a lot, which is very good for India," Jadeja elaborated.Jadeja also reserved praise for Anshul Kamboj, who delivered an economical spell of 2/22 from his 10 overs and walked away with the Player of the Match award.The former India batter acknowledged that Kamboj had faced questions over his bowling during his Test debut against England in 2025, particularly regarding his pace and tendency to bowl no-balls. However, he felt the youngster had shown considerable improvement in Auckland.Jadeja also suggested that Kamboj's workload before the England assignment could have contributed to his struggles, pointing out that fatigue can affect a bowler's execution. His performance against New Zealand, according to Jadeja, reflected better pace, consistency and accuracy."He bowled extremely well. The vision everyone had was that he didn't have pace when he played in England and was bowling a lot of no-balls. I think he had come after playing a lot of cricket then. So a guy also gets tired. It's not that easy. Then he was playing for the first time, but the consistency and the slight increase in his pace he showed today (Wednesday), if we talk about the accuracy amongst the four bowlers, it's Anshul Kamboj," Jadeja added.
Article Summary: India beat New Zealand by five wickets in the first ODI in Auckland. Ajay Jadeja praised Arshdeep Singh's performance, but said he could have avoided expensive final over. Jadeja also praised Anshul Kamboj's bowling, saying he had shown improvement.

Article Title: ‘We weren’t aware’: Mitchell Starc stands by his version of Sandpapergate despite David Warner backing Usman Khawaja
Article Text:
File Pic: Australia's Mitchell Starc and Usman Khawaja (Reuters Photo)

Starc stands by 2021 statement after Warner backs Khawaja

Warner calls Khawaja's revelations '100% accurate'

Cricket Australia rules out fresh investigation

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Australian fast bowler Mitchell Starc has stood by his version of the 2018 ball-tampering scandal, insisting that his recollection of the infamous Sandpapergate episode has not changed, even as former teammate David Warner publicly backed Usman Khawaja's explosive claims about the controversy.Starc's response comes a day after Warner threw his weight behind Khawaja, describing the former Australia opener's revelations as “100% accurate” and questioning the credibility of Cricket Australia's investigation into the incident.Khawaja, in his autobiography Sabr, has claimed that the knowledge of the ball-tampering operation extended beyond the three players who were punished — Steve Smith, Warner and Cameron Bancroft — and that the entire Australian dressing room, including players and support staff, should have accepted collective responsibility.Starc, however, maintained that his position remained consistent with the statement issued by Australia's bowling quartet in 2021, which denied prior knowledge of a foreign object being used to alter the ball.Speaking at an event marking the launch of Australia's summer of cricket, Starc said he had not followed the renewed debate closely but made it clear that his recollection of the events remained unchanged.“I haven't really paid much attention to it to be fair,” Starc said, as quoted by Fox Sports.“Obviously there are differing opinions of eight years ago. We were heavily grilled through the process at the time and since. I won't speak on behalf of the bowlers, but, from where I stand, my opinion hasn't changed, and my recollection hasn't changed from what we said in 2021,” he added.Starc also reiterated that the bowlers were unaware of any foreign substance being taken onto the field to tamper with the ball during the Cape Town Test.“We weren't aware anything was taken on the field to be tampered with. We saw it on the big screen in Cape Town,” he said.In 2021, Starc, Pat Cummins, Josh Hazlewood and Nathan Lyon had issued a joint statement after their integrity was questioned over the scandal. The quartet said they did not know a foreign substance had been taken onto the field until they saw the footage on the stadium's big screen at Newlands.Starc also addressed Khawaja's claim that sandpaper had been used during the preceding Test in Port Elizabeth, now known as Gqeberha. He said he had no prior knowledge of the alleged incident and left it to those making the claims to explain further.Warner, one of the three players handed a 12-month ban by Cricket Australia after the Cape Town incident, publicly backed Khawaja in a video posted on Instagram.“It's been eight years since I've spoken on this topic. And Uzzie (Usman Khawaja), I throw my full support behind you. I thank you for what you've done. It's 100% accurate what you've said. Now everyone knows the truth. It's out there. People wanted to know it; you've come out and said it, and now people are saying, 'Why eight years on?' Talking about selling a book—this is Usman's story. This is what Usman believes,” Warner said.Warner also questioned why Khawaja, who was sitting next to Bancroft during the Cape Town Test, was not interviewed as part of Cricket Australia's investigation.“Now, this whole interview process was rushed and botched. Uzzie was sitting next to Cameron Bancroft; Uzzie was not interviewed. How is that a thorough investigation? It baffles me,” he said.“It's about accountability, transparency, ensuring that the truth is properly examined. And perhaps it's time people stop scrutinising the person asking for accountability and start asking those responsible for the investigation to provide it,” Warner added.He also revealed that the renewed discussion had forced him to explain the events and their aftermath to his daughters, particularly his 12-year-old Ivy, who wanted to know why the family had been surrounded by cameras and why they were crying on television.“That was a hard thing to do. But one thing I did say is, 'Girls, tell the truth, because lies will eventually get out,'” Warner said.He concluded by reiterating his support for Khawaja, saying: “It's been a tough time for my family, Steve and Cameron no doubt, but this is what needed to come out. I fully support that, Uzzie.”The renewed claims have also brought Cricket Australia's original findings back into focus. The board's 2018 investigation concluded that Smith, Warner and Bancroft were involved in the ball-tampering plot, while the other members of the squad were cleared of wrongdoing.Cricket Australia chief executive Todd Greenberg said the governing body would not reopen the investigation despite the fresh revelations in Khawaja's book.“There are specific details in his book that contradict the versions that have been provided by others,” Greenberg said.“We have said we're comfortable with the outcome of the investigation based on the information we've received. That includes what we've seen from Usman, and our position hasn't changed on that.”Greenberg added that Cricket Australia did not see a compelling reason to revisit the matter.
Article Summary: Mitchell Starc stands by his version of the 2018 ball-tampering scandal. Starc insists his recollection of the incident has not changed. Former teammate David Warner has publicly backed Usman Khawaja. Warner calls Khawja's revelations '100% accurate' in his autobiography Sabr.

NEW DELHI: Anshul Kamboj may be experiencing New Zealand conditions for the first time, but the Indian pacer is hardly finding them unfamiliar. The cold weather and seamer-friendly pitches have reminded him of winter in Haryana, where he has been honing his bowling skills since the age of 13. That familiarity appears to be working in his favour, with Kamboj making an impressive start to his maiden ODI assignment in New Zealand.Coming into the playing XI as a change, Kamboj has troubled the New Zealand batters with his accuracy, disciplined line and hard lengths. He returned figures of 2/22 in the first ODI at Eden Park and followed it up with 2/25 in the second match, making an immediate impression with the ball."I started playing when I was 13 years old. I play for Haryana. So it's like similar kind of, what can I say, weather and wickets as well in Haryana," Kamboj told the host broadcasters.Having grown up bowling in conditions similar to those in New Zealand, the 25-year-old has looked comfortable on the bouncy tracks at Auckland's Eden Park and Wellington's Basin Reserve.While the conditions have suited his style, Kamboj is not looking to rely solely on the assistance available from the pitches.The Haryana pacer believes accuracy and adapting to the demands of the surface and match situation remain crucial to his success."It's about accuracy and the perfect line and length, according to the wicket and the situation. It's working for me right now, so I'm just focusing on that," he said.His preparation also included an India A outing, which helped him understand the conditions and identify the right lengths to bowl in New Zealand."Actually, it was just about acclimatising to the weather. The wicket was a bit nippy, and I just wanted to understand the right lengths and the right areas where I need to bowl. I'm just focusing on that," Kamboj explained.The early returns suggest that the preparation has paid off, with his disciplined approach making him an effective option in India's pace attack.Kamboj's impressive international start comes on the back of a breakthrough 2026 IPL season with Chennai Super Kings , where he picked up 21 wickets in 14 matches.The opportunity to be around Mahendra Singh Dhoni and former head coach Stephen Fleming during his CSK stint also contributed to his development. Kamboj described the experience as an important learning phase, stressing that he continues to focus on improving rather than getting carried away by results."Actually, that was a good learning experience for me, and I'm still learning a lot. I'm just making sure that I'm learning in the right way, not thinking too much about the results, but focusing on what I need to do and what I need to do on the field as well," he said.For Kamboj, representing India has been another special milestone, particularly after years of working his way through domestic cricket."Actually, I'm excited and very happy as well, as I'm playing for my national team. It's everyone's dream to play for their national team, so it's pretty much exciting," he said.With two impressive performances already behind him, Kamboj will look to carry his accuracy and confidence into the remainder of the New Zealand tour.

NEW DELHI: Former India head coach Ravi Shastri feels coaching is tougher than playing cricket or working as a commentator. He said the job comes with huge responsibility and pressure, as a coach has little control over what happens once the players step onto the field.Known for his straight-talking nature and energetic commentary, Shastri shared his views on the three roles in an interview with Sky Sport's Ian Smith.When asked which one he found the toughest, the former India coach picked coaching."Yeah, the toughest would be coaching, right. See, no, because you are nothing in your control once the players leave and get onto the field. You have the bat, ball when you're playing, the mic when you're broadcasting. But once the players go out, you know, you can only twiddle your thumbs. And it comes with immense responsibility. You know, the expectations of the country are such. COVID, no COVID, you got to win, you know, game after game. So there's no hiding behind that," Shastri said.He also spoke about the pressure that comes with the job and the satisfaction of delivering results."You know, you always have the gun to your head. But if you pull it off and you're successful, I mean, then the rewards, it's very rewarding.Gives you tons of respect. And, you know, makes you enjoy what you're doing and gives you that kind of job satisfaction with nothing else gave you," he said.Shastri was India's head coach from July 2017 to November 2021. His tenure saw the team achieve several major milestones, including two historic Test series victories in Australia.India won their first-ever Test series in Australia during the 2018-19 Border-Gavaskar Trophy. They followed it up with another memorable 2-1 series win in 2020-21, despite several injury setbacks.Under Shastri, India also held the No. 1 position in the ICC Test rankings for 42 months and reached the final of the inaugural World Test Championship in 2021. The team also made it to the semi-finals of the 2019 ODI World Cup.Shastri also looked back at his journey in broadcasting and spoke about what has kept him connected to cricket for so many years.He said his passion for the game has been the biggest reason behind his long association with the sport, despite having opportunities to explore other fields."[On his journey into broadcasting] it's amazing how life can take you in various places. And particularly the cricketing life. I mean it's captured us. I mean obviously you love the game. I mean you know to stay involved because you would have had many, many opportunities to break away and do other things with your stature in India.But you stayed with the game. And I love it. I mean the only way we can hang in here if we are passionate about the game," Shastri said."If you're not passionate about the game, you don't love the game, you won't be here this long with showing that kind of enthusiasm for every game day after day. You know, whether it's with you, the way you commentated on that World Cup final, you know, a close finish, you were calling it at the end. Fabulous. And we've called many finals in the end, you know, right through our careers. And it's a privilege, you know, when someone understands the game, understands the discipline of television, you know, and then to work that for that length of time. It's fun," he said.
Article Summary: Former India head coach Ravi Shastri says coaching is tougher than playing cricket or working as a commentator. He said the job comes with huge responsibility and pressure, as a coach has little control over what happens once the players step onto the field. He also spoke about the pressure that comes with the job and the satisfaction of delivering results.

Article Title: Best ever! From 14 medals to 114: How India achieved more with fewer athletes at the Asian Para Games
Article Text:

From 14 medals to 114: India's remarkable rise

India's Asian Para Games record

Smaller contingent, bigger return

Hangzhou vs Aichi-Nagoya

Image credit: TimesofIndia.com

Athletics powers India's medal surge

India's leading medal-winning sports in Asian Para Games 2026

Multiple medallists underline India's depth

Paralympic progress provides the wider context

Fourth place sets a new benchmark

From 14 medals in 2010 to 114 in 2026, India’s remarkable rise continued in Aichi-Nagoya as a smaller contingent surpassed its previous best, achieved 30 gold medals and secured its highest-ever finish at the continental para-sport showpiece.India’s campaign at the Asian Para Games 2026 was a triumph that few would have predicted when the size of the contingent became known. With just 167 athletes travelling to Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, the prospect of repeating the 100-plus medal haul achieved at Hangzhou in 2023 appeared ambitious. The previous edition had seen India send more than 300 athletes to the competition, returning with a record 108 medals after subsequent revisions to the original tally.But the Indian contingent defied expectations, producing an even bigger return with significantly fewer athletes. India finished the fifth edition of the Asian Para Games with 114 medals — 30 gold, 35 silver and 49 bronze — to secure fourth place, both the highest medal tally and the best finish in the country's history at the event.The numbers tell a compelling story of progress. India improved its medal tally for the fifth consecutive edition, added to its gold-medal record and finished ahead of South Korea, which had threatened to challenge its position in the final standings.More than the record itself, the achievement highlighted how far India's para-sport movement has travelled in 16 years — from a modest 14-medal return at the inaugural edition in 2010 to a fourth-place finish among Asia's leading para-sport nations.India's progress at the Asian Para Games has been steady, with each edition bringing a new high in the overall medal tally.At Guangzhou in 2010, India won 14 medals — one gold, four silver and nine bronze — to finish 15th. The 2014 edition in Incheon brought a substantial improvement, with the country collecting 33 medals, including three gold, but remaining 15th in the standings.The breakthrough arrived at Jakarta in 2018. India's medal tally rose to 72, comprising 15 gold, 24 silver and 33 bronze, while its position improved to ninth.Hangzhou in 2023 marked another major leap. India crossed the 100-medal barrier for the first time, initially returning with 111 medals before the tally was revised to 108 following a doping-related disqualification and a medal reallocation. The revised haul comprised 27 gold, 32 silver and 49 bronze, with India eventually classified sixth.Aichi-Nagoya extended that upward trajectory. India added six medals to its revised Hangzhou total, increased its gold-medal count from 27 to 30 and climbed two places to fourth.The numbers at a glance: India's medal tally increased more than eightfold between 2010 and 2026. Its gold-medal count grew from one to 30, while its position improved from 15th to fourth.The rise has not been limited to the overall tally. India has improved its standing in three successive editions since 2014, moving from 15th to ninth, then sixth and now fourth. The 2026 result represents the culmination of a sustained upward trend rather than an isolated breakthrough.The most striking feature of India's latest performance was the efficiency with which its athletes converted participation into medals.India fielded 167 athletes — 111 men and 56 women — across 11 sports at Aichi-Nagoya. That was considerably fewer than the 309 athletes listed for the Hangzhou campaign in 2023, yet the team surpassed its previous best by six medals.The comparison is revealing. India sent approximately 46 per cent fewer athletes than it did to Hangzhou, but its medal tally increased by nearly six per cent. The gold-medal count rose by three, the silver tally by three, and the bronze count remained unchanged.On a simple medals-per-athlete measure, India's return increased from approximately 0.35 medals per athlete in Hangzhou to 0.68 in Aichi-Nagoya. This is an aggregate comparison, not an individual success rate, since athletes can win multiple medals and the number of events and opportunities varies across sports.Nevertheless, the figures underline the scale of the achievement. A smaller squad did not merely match the previous edition's success; it established a new benchmark for Indian para-sport.Para-athletics was the backbone of India's campaign, delivering 65 medals — 22 gold, 19 silver and 24 bronze. That represented nearly 57 per cent of the country's overall tally and made athletics the single biggest contributor to India's fourth-place finish.Para-badminton followed with 16 medals, including three gold, five silver and eight bronze. Together, athletics and badminton accounted for 81 medals, more than 70 per cent of India's total.Swimming contributed 11 medals, comprising three silver and eight bronze. Archery added six medals, including three gold and three silver, while shooting produced five, with two gold, two silver and one bronze.Athletics' contribution also illustrates how India's progress has accelerated. At Hangzhou, para-athletics produced 52 medals, including 16 gold, 17 silver and 19 bronze. In Aichi-Nagoya, the discipline's haul rose to 65, with six additional gold medals.Badminton's contribution was different. India won 21 medals in the sport at Hangzhou, including four gold, but finished with 16 in 2026. Instead, the substantial gains in athletics and the contributions from other sports helped compensate for the decline in badminton medals.That distinction matters: the record haul reflects both the strength of India's established medal-winning disciplines and the need to broaden its success across events in future editions.India's record was supported by athletes who delivered more than once during the competition. A total of 26 Indian athletes won multiple medals, while six athletes collected multiple gold medals, demonstrating the importance of individual excellence in a campaign involving 11 sports.Archer Sheetal Devi was among the standout performers, winning two gold medals and a silver. Her two golds came in the mixed compound and individual compound events, while the silver added to her three-medal haul.Athletics provided several other multiple gold medallists. Dilip Gavit, Nishad Kumar, Pranav Soorma and Simran Sharma each won two gold medals, while shooting contributed through Mona Agarwal, who also secured two golds.Four athletes finished with three medals apiece: Sheetal Devi in archery, Thulasimathi Murugesan in badminton, Ravi Budigina in swimming and Himanshu Nandal in swimming. Their performances illustrated how athletes winning across multiple events can make a significant difference to a country's final tally.The figures also invite comparison with Hangzhou, where 25 Indian athletes won multiple medals. The increase to 26 in 2026 was modest, but the overall tally improved despite a much smaller contingent. The result points to a campaign in which medal-winning performances were concentrated among a relatively small squad.India's rise at the Asian Para Games has coincided with a significant improvement at the Paralympics, strengthening the country's standing in international para-sport.At Rio 2016, India won four medals and finished 43rd. Tokyo 2020 marked a breakthrough, with 19 medals — five gold, eight silver and six bronze — lifting India to 24th. At Paris 2024, India recorded its best Paralympic haul of 29 medals, comprising seven gold, nine silver and 13 bronze, to finish 18th.The progression at the Paralympics mirrors the broader trend at the Asian Para Games: larger medal returns, more gold medals and improvements in the standings.India's able-bodied contingent had also finished fourth at the 2026 Asian Games, although its 85-medal tally was below the 106 medals achieved at Hangzhou in 2023. The para contingent's performance offered a contrasting story of growth, with its medal count rising and its position improving.China dominated Aichi-Nagoya, finishing with 435 medals, including 207 gold. Hosts Japan were second with 186 medals, while Uzbekistan finished third with 145. India placed fourth with 114, ahead of South Korea, which collected 100 medals, including 29 gold.India's final position was not guaranteed until the closing stages. South Korea remained within reach, but its final-day return of one gold and two silver left it one gold behind India. The Indian contingent held on to fourth place with 30 gold, 35 silver and 49 bronze.The gap to third-placed Uzbekistan shows that further progress will require India to expand its medal-winning strength across disciplines. Yet the immediate achievement is significant: India has moved from 15th at the first two editions to fourth, while increasing its tally at every successive Games.The challenge now is to sustain that momentum, build a deeper pool of competitive athletes and reduce dependence on a handful of disciplines.For a contingent of just 167 athletes, 114 medals represent more than a record. They mark the latest step in a 16-year transformation of Indian para-sport — one that began with 14 medals in Guangzhou and has now culminated in a historic fourth-place finish in Aichi-Nagoya.
Article Summary: India fielded 167 athletes — 111 men and 56 women — across 11 sports at Aichi- Nagoya. India finished the fifth edition of the Asian Para Games with 114 medals — 30 gold, 35 silver and 49 bronze — to secure fourth place. It is the best finish in the country's history at the event.

NEW DELHI: Suhas Yathiraj was disappointed with his bronze medal at the Asian Para Games in Nagoya. Having beaten Indonesia's Fredy Setiawan in their group match just days earlier, the Indian shuttler had hoped to reach the final and fight for gold.Suhas lost the men's singles SL4 semifinal 23-21, 8-21, 15-21. He had chances to take the opening game but failed to convert them. After bouncing back to win the second game 21-8, he lost focus at a crucial stage of the decider.“Definitely not satisfied with bronze. I think if I had played up to my full potential, I would have definitely done better. In fact, I defeated Fredy of Indonesia in the group match in Nagoya only a few days ago,” Suhas told TimesofIndia.com from Aichi-Nagoya in Japan.“In the semifinal match, the first set was very close. I lost 23-21 and I had game point, set point, but I couldn't convert that. In the second set, I won very easily. In the third set, I think after 10-all, I sort of lost focus for two to three rallies. That is where he took the game. So, it was not my best day, I would assume. I would always love to win a gold medal. So, yes, I am a little sad from that angle,” he said.The defeat also reminded him of how important it is to perform under pressure at major tournaments.“It is the most important factor to win medals at major games because you might be training well, you might actually have the fitness and the skills. But if you don't recreate that during the major games, then probably it is of not much use in terms of professional success,” Suhas said.Suhas, an IAS officer, said he had never imagined representing India in international badminton a decade ago.In November 2016, he made his debut at the Asian Championships in Beijing and won gold. Since then, he has won several medals at major international events. These include bronze at the 2018 Asian Para Games in Jakarta, silver at the Tokyo 2020 Paralympics, another silver at the Paris 2024 Paralympics, gold at the Hangzhou Asian Para Games and bronze in Nagoya.The 43-year-old has represented India at two Paralympic Games, Tokyo in 2020 and Paris in 2024, winning silver on both occasions.With the Los Angeles 2028 Paralympics approaching, the big question is whether he can go one step further and win gold.The desire is there, but Suhas is not looking too far ahead. He wants to take things one step at a time.“If you had asked me 10 years ago, I didn't even know that I would play for India. But whenever I look at the medals and the love I have got from fans and sportspersons around the world, the journey has been quite satisfying. I have had the honour of wearing the Indian jersey and winning medals for my country,” he said.“I am grateful for what God has given me. I never imagined that I would become an IAS officer one day, an Arjuna awardee or a badminton player winning medals for India. I never imagined all this. But thanks to the Almighty for all these,” Suhas, who is also an Arjuna Award recipient, said.“So if God and destiny have been kind to me, I hope they will take me to a place that I deserve. I hope I can do the best that I can in whatever I choose to,” he added.For most people, the end of a hectic working day is a time to relax, spend time with family, play with their children or watch a movie.For Suhas, it is often time to pick up his badminton racket and head to the court. His day includes early-morning gym sessions, office work, inspections, meetings, video conferences and checking files. Despite his demanding responsibilities as an IAS officer, he makes time for badminton and follows a strict fitness routine to compete at the highest level.Balancing the two careers is not easy, but his love for the sport keeps him going.“If you choose what you love, then the journey becomes painless. You enjoy that journey. That's what I do,” Suhas said.Explaining how he manages his work and training, he said: “It is challenging. My training generally starts in the night and it always involves sacrifices. Probably others would be spending time with their family members or having leisure time. My leisure time is to play badminton. In badminton, you need an extremely high level of fitness. It's challenging, hectic but at the same time I love it.”“I don't remember eating sweets in the last many months. I can't recall when I had my last sweet. So, I almost don't eat sweets or fried food and am also quite conscious about the nutrition that I take,” he said.Suhas grew up watching Malaysian badminton great Lee Chong Wei and was inspired by his movement on the court.“Yes, I have always been inspired by so many top players in the able-bodied category. Growing up, I watched the matches of Lee Chong Wei and how he used to move around the court,” he said.“Even in India, the top shuttlers perform extremely well, whether it is Lakshya Sen, HS Prannoy or Kidambi Srikanth. I know them personally and have always admired how well they are able to compete at the top,” Suhas signed off.

NEW DELHI: India signed off from the Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Asian Para Games with their best-ever medal haul of 114 medals as the week-long continental competition concluded with a closing ceremony at the Mizuho Park Athletics Stadium in Nagoya, Japan, on Saturday.Double gold medallists Nishad Kumar and Mona Agarwal led the Indian contingent as flag-bearers at the ceremony, marking the end of a landmark campaign in which the country's para-athletes delivered historic victories, world-record performances and podium sweeps across disciplines.India finished fourth in the overall standings with 30 gold, 35 silver and 49 bronze medals, surpassing its previous best of 108 medals at the 2022 Hangzhou Games.Held in Japan for the first time, the fifth edition of the Asian Para Games brought together around 4,000 athletes and staff from 45 countries and regions. Thulasimathi enjoyed a memorable campaign of her own , combining with Manasi Joshi to win gold in women's doubles SL3-SU5. The Indian pair beat China's Yang Qiuxia and Xiao Zuxian 21-16, 21-13 in the final.The 24-year-old also secured silver in women's singles SU5 after losing 18-21, 11-21 to Yang in the final, completing a three-medal haul.Shooter Mona Agarwal added another golden chapter to India's campaign, shattering the world record to win the women's 50m rifle 3 positions SH1 title with a score of 357.5 points.The 38-year-old had earlier won the women's 10m air rifle standing SH1 gold with a Games-record score of 250.0 points, edging compatriot Avani Lekhara, who took silver with 249.6.Mona's latest triumph gave her a second gold of the Games and further underlined her standing among India's leading para-shooters. She had also secured India's first 2028 Paralympic quota earlier this year.In archery, Paralympic champion Harvinder Singh teamed up with debutant Vijay Sundi to win the men's recurve doubles gold, defeating China's Yun Duo and Zhao Lixue 5-1 in the final.India's women's recurve doubles pair of Bhawna Choudhary and Pooja Jatyan settled for silver after losing 0-6 to China's Gao Zihan and Wang Xueqian.India's swimmers also exceeded expectations, finishing the Games with 11 medals, including three silver. Himanshu Nandal completed a hat-trick of bronze medals by finishing third in the men's 100m freestyle S11. The 22-year-old, who was born blind due to optic nerve failure, clocked 1:05.90, behind Japan's Uchu Tomita (58.22) and China's Chuanzhen Sun (58.70).Nandal had earlier won bronze in the men's 400m freestyle and 100m breaststroke S11 events. Ravi Budigina also finished with three medals, comprising two silver and one bronze.With nine gold medals on Friday and a record overall haul of 114, India signed off from its Asian Para Games campaign with its most successful performance at the continental event, surpassing the benchmark set in Hangzhou three years ago.
Article Summary: India's para-athletes produced a spectacular finish to their campaign at the Asian Para Games. The country's final tally of 30 gold, 35 silver and 49 bronze surpassed its previous best of 108 medals, including 27 gold, achieved at the Hangzhou Games in 2023. India's badminton contingent delivered three gold medals, led by Paris Paralympic champion Nitesh Kumar.

Article Title: Asian Para Games: Sumit Antil leads India's javelin 1-2-3 as Pranav Soorma strikes gold again
Article Text:
Sumit Antil and Pranav Soorma (ANI/PTI Photo)

Sumit Antil leads India's javelin sweep

Pranav Soorma defends club throw crown

NEW DELHI: India enjoyed a golden double in para-athletics at the Asian Para Games on Friday, with star javelin thrower Sumit Antil leading a podium sweep and Pranav Soorma defending his title in the men's club throw F51 event.Antil successfully defended his gold in the men's javelin throw F42-44/61-64 combined event, while Mahendra Gurjar and Sandip Sanjay Sargar completed an all-Indian podium finish. Soorma, meanwhile, added another gold to his collection with a Games-record performance in the club throw.The results added to India's medal haul as the country's para-athletes continued to deliver strong performances in Aichi-Nagoya.The 28-year-old Antil, a two-time Paralympic gold medallist and world record holder, produced a best throw of 72.46m in his second attempt to claim gold.Although he could not surpass his personal best, Antil was comfortably ahead of the field while competing in the F64 classification. He had won gold at the 2023 Asian Para Games with a then-world-record throw of 73.29m before improving the mark to 74.82m in May this year.Gurjar secured silver with a throw of 59.03m, while Sargar took bronze with an effort of 64.48m.Despite Sargar recording the longer distance, Gurjar finished ahead because of his superior Raza points score, which is used to determine rankings in combined events involving athletes from different classifications.The F42, F44, F62 and F64 categories are combined in certain field events, including javelin and discus throw, to create a larger and more competitive field. The classifications cover athletes with lower-limb impairments, with some competing without prostheses and others using them.Soorma continued India's gold rush by successfully defending his men's club throw F51 title with a Games-record effort of 32.87m.The Indian had won gold in the same event at the previous edition of the Asian Para Games and claimed silver at the 2024 Paris Paralympics.South Korea's Jiwon Jung took silver with a personal-best throw of 28.40m, while Dharamvir secured bronze with 27.71m to give India another double podium finish.The F51 classification is for athletes with significant movement limitations affecting the trunk, legs and hands, with varying degrees of impairment in arm movement. Competitors perform their throws from a seated position.With Antil leading a historic Indian sweep in the javelin and Soorma retaining his title, India's para-athletes delivered another memorable day in Aichi-Nagoya.
Article Summary: Sumit Antil leads India's javelin sweep at the Asian Para Games. Pranav Soorma defends his title in the men's club throw F51 event. Mahendra Gurjar and Sandip Sanjay Sargar complete all-Indian podium finish.

Nishad Kumar and Mona Agarwal (Pic credit: X)

Mona's record-breaking run in shooting

NEW DELHI: Double gold medallists Mona Agarwal and Nishad Kumar will be India's flag-bearers at the closing ceremony of the 2026 Asian Para Games in Aichi-Nagoya on Saturday, following outstanding campaigns in shooting and para-athletics.Both athletes won two gold medals each at the continental event, with Mona producing a record-breaking performance in shooting and Nishad excelling in the high jump and long jump.Their selection as flag-bearers recognises their achievements as India prepare to bring the Games to a close.The 38-year-old Mona opened India's medal account in shooting by winning gold in the women's 10m air rifle standing SH1 event with a Games-record score of 250.0 points. Article Title: Who is Himanshu Nandal? The para-swimmer who won a hat-trick of bronze medals at Asian Para Games in Japan
Article Text:
Himanshu Nandal (PTI Photo)

Who is Himanshu Nandal?

From Paris Paralympics qualification to Asian Para Games medals

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Indian para-swimmer Himanshu Nandal made his mark at the Asian Para Games 2026 in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, completing a hat-trick of bronze medals with another podium finish in the men's 100m freestyle S11 event on Friday.The 22-year-old clocked 1 minute 5.90 seconds to finish third, behind Japan's Uchu Tomita, who won gold in a Games-record time of 58.22 seconds, and China's Chuanzhen Sun, who took silver in 58.70 seconds.Nandal's latest medal added to his earlier bronze finishes in the men's 400m freestyle and 100m breaststroke S11 events. He became one of India's standout performers in para swimming, matching compatriot Ravi Budigina's three-medal haul at the Games, which comprised two silver medals and a bronze.Born blind due to optic nerve failure, Nandal grew up in a sports-oriented family in Rohtak, Haryana. His father had played hockey at the national level, and sport became part of his life from an early age.At four, Nandal moved to Delhi and joined the National Association for the Blind, where he learnt Braille. He initially took up judo and went on to win medals at the national level before switching to swimming in 2021.The change opened a new chapter in his sporting journey, as he quickly progressed from domestic competitions to the international stage.Nandal achieved a significant milestone in 2024 when he became the first Indian blind swimmer to meet the Minimum Qualification Standard for the Paris Paralympics.A political science graduate from the University of Delhi's Atma Ram Sanatan Dharma College, he continued to build his experience against international opposition. In 2025, he reached two finals at the World Para Swimming Championships in Singapore.At the Asian Para Games, Nandal began his medal-winning run on Tuesday, clocking 5:10.91 to secure bronze in the men's 400m freestyle S11 event. He followed it up with another third-place finish in the 100m breaststroke before completing his hat-trick in the 100m freestyle on Friday.The S11 classification is for swimmers with visual impairment, including those with very low visual acuity or no light perception.Nandal's three-medal campaign in Japan marks another milestone in his progress as an Indian para-swimmer and adds to his growing experience at major international competitions.
Article Summary: Himanshu Nandal completes hat-trick of bronze medals at Asian Para Games 2026. The 22-year-old finished third in the men's 100m freestyle S11 event on Friday. Nandal is the first Indian blind swimmer to meet the Minimum Qualification Standard for the Paris Paralympics.

The Indian pair wrapped up the contest in just 28 minutes.Thulasimathi had earlier settled for silver in the women's singles SU5 final, losing 18-21, 11-21 to China's Yang. So this time, winning it and again winning in two sets against Pramod is, of course, very special, and I think it's one of the rarest of the rare things to see," Nitesh said after his victory.Naveen Sivakumar added another gold for India, beating Indonesia's Fredy Setiawan 21-9, 21-17 in the men's singles SL4 final. Paris Paralympic silver medallist defeats China's Yang Qiuxia and Xiao Zuxian 21-16, 21-13 in women's doubles final.
