Article Title: In 2023, England captain Harry Kane shocked property experts by buying a £6.5m Surrey estate only to completely demolish luxury home instead of renovating it for new £20m mega-mansion
Article Text:
England's Harry Kane (9) celebrates after scoring a goal during the World Cup Group L soccer match between England and Croatia in Arlington, Texas, near Dallas, Wednesday, June 17, 2026. (AP Photo/Tony Gutierrez)

A £20 million mansion in Surrey

Life in Munich and another multimillion-pound home

The cars in Kane's collection

The season that brought football's biggest individual prize

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

London, Oct 27 (IANS) England captain Harry Kane has won the 2026 Ballon d'Or in a ceremony at the London Palladium Theatre.

Harry Kane has spent much of his career pursuing the biggest prizes in football, but his latest achievements have also given him the means to build a life far removed from the demands of the pitch. From a £20 million mansion taking shape on one of England’s most exclusive private estates to a collection of luxury cars that reflects his preference for British engineering, the Bayern Munich striker’s lifestyle offers a glimpse of what he has built beyond the game. His extraordinary 2025–26 season, which ended with the Ballon d’Or, has only added to that picture.Kane’s most ambitious property investment is taking shape on the Wentworth Estate in Surrey, an exclusive residential development known for its large private homes and proximity to the countryside. The England captain purchased the land and an existing property in 2023 for a reported £6.5 million, the same year he left Tottenham for Bayern Munich. Rather than renovate the original house, he opted for a complete rebuild.The finished property is expected to be worth around £20 million. Its design follows a neo-Georgian style, with symmetrical architecture, grand windows and imposing pillars around the entrance.The exterior has reportedly prompted comparisons with Buckingham Palace, with one neighbour describing its appearance as resembling the royal residence.The scale of the project extends well beyond its exterior. Planning documents reportedly detail an underground leisure complex featuring a private cinema, swimming pool, bar, treatment room and fully equipped gym. The property is also expected to have four main bedrooms, alongside additional en-suite accommodation for guests and staff.Its underground garage is designed to accommodate five cars, with a rotating platform reportedly costing around £20,000. The system allows vehicles to be turned around without requiring drivers to reverse through the garage.The estate is close to Chelsea's Cobham training ground, although Kane currently lives in Germany while playing for Bayern. The Surrey property is widely viewed as a long-term family home, potentially providing a base in England after his time in Munich.Kane's move to Germany in 2023 did not mean leaving luxury property behind. While representing Bayern, he has reportedly been staying in a hilltop mansion in Grünwald, one of Munich's wealthiest suburbs, valued at nearly £30 million.The property provides a home for Kane and his family during his time in Germany, while the Surrey development represents a substantial investment in his future back in England. Together, the two residences reflect the financial position he has established after years at the highest level of professional football.Kane's taste in cars has generally favoured established British marques rather than the more conspicuous supercars often associated with elite footballers. His collection has been linked to a Range Rover, Jaguar F-Pace, Jaguar F-Type and Bentley Continental GT Supersports.The Bentley has been among the most notable vehicles associated with the striker. Purchased in 2020, the white Continental GT Supersports featured black 21-inch alloy wheels. Kane described it as “a beautiful, beautiful car” and his first proper sports car. The model costs more than £200,000 new, although his vehicle has since reportedly been listed for sale.In Munich, his daily transport has taken a more practical direction. Bayern's sponsorship arrangement with Audi provides cars for the club's players, and Kane reportedly selected a black Audi Q8 e-tron.Kane's lifestyle investments have accompanied a career that reached a new peak in 2025–26. The striker scored 61 goals and provided seven assists in 51 appearances across all competitions for Bayern, earning the Ballon d'Or in London.His Bundesliga return was particularly impressive: 36 goals and five assists in 31 appearances. He also scored 10 times in six DFB-Pokal matches, added 14 goals and two assists in 13 Champions League appearances, and found the net once in the Franz Beckenbauer Supercup. Across the season, he scored approximately once every 66 minutes.Kane began the campaign with a goal in the Supercup before scoring a hat-trick against RB Leipzig on the opening day of the Bundesliga season. He later reached 100 goals for Bayern against Werder Bremen in September, becoming the fastest player in the club's 126-year history to reach that milestone.A further hat-trick against Hoffenheim preceded another standout performance against Stuttgart, where he collected the ball near halfway, advanced into space and struck a powerful shot from around 25 yards. In Europe, his 14 Champions League goals saw him share the competition's top-scorer honour with Kylian Mbappé. Kane also scored against Real Madrid in a dramatic quarter-final tie that produced 10 goals across two legs.The Ballon d'Or made him the first Englishman to win the men's award since Michael Owen in 2001, and the first Bayern Munich player to claim it since Karl-Heinz Rummenigge in 1981. For a player who had finished 13th in the previous year's voting, the recognition marked a remarkable change in his individual standing.Kane's property and car investments offer a picture of the life he has built away from football, but his latest season explains the financial and sporting position that has made those ambitions possible.
Article Summary: England captain Harry Kane has won the 2026 Ballon d'Or. The 25-year-old scored 61 goals and provided seven assists in 51 appearances for Bayern Munich in 2025–26. Kane's most ambitious property investment is taking shape on the Wentworth Estate in Surrey. While representing Bayern, he has reportedly been staying in a hilltop mansion in Grünwald valued at nearly £30 million.

Article Title: Ex-Spurs star Dele Alli wears Arsenal shirt after losing bet to iShowSpeed, then burns rival jersey to appease Tottenham fans
Article Text:
Dele Alli wears an Arsenal shirt after losing an EAFC 27 challenge to iShowSpeed, before seemingly destroying it to appease Spurs fans/ Image: Instagram

Dele Alli loses bet to iShowSpeed and wears Arsenal shirt

Dele Alli's livestreams and his search for a football comeback

From Tottenham star to an uncertain future

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Dele Alli risked upsetting Tottenham supporters after losing a pair of EAFC 27 matches against streamer iShowSpeed and fulfilling a forfeit that required him to wear an Arsenal shirt. The former England international apologised to his former club's fans before appearing to get rid of the shirt in a follow-up Instagram post, turning the incident into another moment of entertainment during his search for a return to professional football.Alli, who spent seven years at Tottenham between 2015 and 2022, agreed to wear an Arsenal shirt if he lost a series of matches against YouTuber and streamer iShowSpeed during a livestream.The pair faced each other in EAFC 27, with Alli taking control of Paris Saint-Germain in the opening game against Speed's Bayern Munich. The 30-year-old was beaten 7-2 before switching teams for the rematch, choosing Al Qadsiah against Speed's Al Nassr. He lost that match 4-2, leaving him with no choice but to honour the forfeit.Alli subsequently shared a photograph of himself wearing an Arsenal jersey on his Instagram story, acknowledging the reaction it would provoke among Tottenham supporters.“Sorry Spurs fans, but a bet is a bet,” he wrote.The midfielder, who remains closely associated with Tottenham after his seven-year spell in north London, later appeared to make amends with another post. He shared a photograph of the Arsenal shirt looking ripped up on the floor, with a fire extinguisher placed beside it, suggesting that he had burned the jersey.“Speed, a bet is a bet! But this is what you call the aftermath,” Alli wrote.The posts gave Tottenham supporters a glimpse of the lighter side of his recent online activity, although the sight of their former player wearing Arsenal colours was unlikely to have been welcomed by everyone at the club.The appearance with Speed was not Alli's first involvement in livestreams since becoming a free agent. On another occasion, he contacted several former teammates during a broadcast, allowing viewers to listen to the conversations.One of the calls involved former Tottenham teammate Harry Kane. Alli backed the England captain to win the 2026 Ballon d'Or weeks before Kane went on to claim the award in London.His growing presence online has also brought renewed attention to the contrast between his current circumstances and the heights he reached during his career at Tottenham.Alli has been without a club since September 2025, when his contract with Italian side Como was terminated. He has not appeared in English football since 2024 and is still attempting to find a route back into the professional game.He had been using the training facilities at League Two club Barnet as he worked towards a comeback. It also emerged that Salford City had offered him the opportunity to join the club under then-manager Karl Robinson, although the proposed move never materialised. Alli was subsequently pictured training with semi-professional side Windsor & Eton.His last competitive appearance came in March 2025, when he made his Como debut against AC Milan. The midfielder was sent off just nine minutes after coming on, in what was his first senior appearance in almost 750 days.The difficulties of Alli's recent career stand in sharp contrast to the player who became one of the Premier League's most exciting young midfielders.He scored 67 goals in 269 appearances for Tottenham between 2015 and 2022, winning the PFA Young Player of the Year award twice. He was also part of the side that finished second in the Premier League in 2017 and reached the Champions League final in 2019.His performances during that period established him as one of England's most promising attacking midfielders, but his career subsequently lost momentum, with injuries, changes of club and limited playing opportunities interrupting his progress.At 30, Alli is still targeting a return to competitive football, although he has yet to secure a club or establish when he might play again. His livestream appearance with Speed offered a glimpse of what he has been doing away from the pitch, while the search for his next footballing opportunity continues.

Bryson DeChambeau has spoken publicly for the first time since LIV Golf confirmed it would wind down operations, reflecting on his four years with the Saudi-backed league while leaving his own future unresolved. The two-time US Open champion stopped short of confirming whether he intends to return to the PGA Tour or join the DP World Tour, with a key membership deadline approaching.DeChambeau joined LIV Golf in 2022, becoming one of the most prominent players to leave the established professional circuit for the breakaway league. His decision came during a period of significant upheaval in men's golf, when players including Brooks Koepka, Dustin Johnson and Phil Mickelson also accepted reported eight- and nine-figure contracts to join the Saudi-backed competition.The defections triggered a prolonged dispute between LIV Golf and the established tours. The PGA Tour and European Tour initially imposed restrictions on players who had joined the breakaway circuit, although some of those rules have since been relaxed.Following LIV Golf's announcement that it would cease operations, DeChambeau issued a statement reflecting on his time with the league without expressing regret over his decision.“I’m not going to rewrite the past four years,” he said.“I made a decision I believed in, and I’m grateful for what came with it: playing in front of fans new and old around the world who rarely got to see the best players at home.”He singled out Adelaide in Australia and Johannesburg in South Africa among the destinations that made a lasting impression during his time with LIV Golf.The American also defended the league's team format, which he believes remains a worthwhile concept even if its future structure changes. LIV Golf's tournaments featured 57 players divided into 13 teams, with separate individual and team competitions, before the season concluded with a bracket-style team championship involving singles and alternate-shot matches.“I still believe in team golf,” DeChambeau said. “It may look different in the future, but I still believe it’s essential to growing the game.”He added that he had given everything he could to make the format work during his time with the league.While DeChambeau made clear that his commitment to growing the sport remains unchanged, he offered no confirmation about where he intends to compete once LIV Golf shuts down.His immediate schedule includes the Nedbank Golf Challenge in December, Gary Player's tournament in South Africa. DeChambeau said he was looking forward to returning after the reception he received during his first visit to the country.“In December, I’ll compete at the Nedbank Golf Challenge, Gary Player’s event, in front of fans who made my first visit to South Africa unforgettable. Beyond that, I’ll go about whatever is next the right way,” he said.“My passion is to grow this game. That’s still the goal. Thank you for sticking with me. Together we can grow this great game we all love.”The question of his longer-term future remains significant because DeChambeau has until November 15 to declare his intention to become a member of the DP World Tour. Missing that deadline could leave him without a straightforward route back into the established professional circuits, potentially limiting his opportunities beyond the major championships.DeChambeau is among the most recognisable figures in modern golf, with nine PGA Tour victories and two US Open titles. He won his first major at Winged Foot in 2020 before claiming a second at Pinehurst in 2024.LIV Golf's shutdown followed the withdrawal of financial backing from Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund. The league had been unable to secure the additional investment required to proceed with its proposed LIV 2.0 plans for 2027, and confirmed in US bankruptcy court on Thursday that it would wind down operations.For DeChambeau, the immediate commitment is South Africa. What follows will depend on the decisions he makes as the breakaway league's players begin considering their next steps.
Article Summary: Bryson DeChambeau has spoken publicly for the first time since LIV Golf confirmed it would wind down operations. The two-time US Open champion stopped short of confirming whether he intends to return to the PGA Tour or join the DP World Tour. The American defended the league's team format, which he believes remains a worthwhile concept even if its future structure changes.
